main_body: Large leafy tree canopy with a short dark trunk and spreading roots, drawn as a clump of foliage with light and dark green patches
top_band: none: the canopy is a mottled mass of light and mid greens with no distinct lighter top band separated from a front face by a step or an edge line
evidence: The tree is organic foliage. The column scan shows light (L=129) and mid (L=68) green patches alternating irregularly, with no consistent top band above a face. The canopy is a rounded volume, as in the Beodeul tree references, and reads as one mass lit from above. For an organic canopy this is acceptable and the kind matches. The trunk and roots are in the lower area, with no plate or flat cap. Nothing in the drawing is a front elevation, side elevation or top-down slab.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours in total (near-black outline, dark green, light green, dark brown) against 427 and 567 for the references, and a median of 4 colours per tile against about 108. All dark edge pixels are neutral (100%), so the outline is a uniform near-black sticker line instead of a dark tone of the adjacent material. Shading has only 2 greens plus a trunk brown, with no highlight, no mid steps and no per-clump shading. The leaf pattern is a dithered two-tone checkering rather than clumps in several greens. Flat-fill coverage is low (4%) only because the two tones are scattered, not because the surface is rich. Next to the references, it looks much thinner and flatter.
